business_problem: Imgix's private data centers lacked the elasticity and capacity to process thousands of concurrent, just-in-time image and video transformation requests. Maintaining physical infrastructure also diverted its lean engineering team from product development, while slow processing could affect customer experiences.
solution_summary: Imgix accepts customer requests for just-in-time image and video transformation, avoiding pre-rendering and storing every asset variant. Its core workload runs on Compute Engine G4 VMs with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, processing concurrent pixel-manipulation tasks and serving the resulting media; Imgix reports it changed virtually no application code. Gemini models assess whether a request needs an AI feature before triggering more expensive vision processing, supporting smart cropping and highlight extraction. Cloud Storage provides a dedicated cache for video assets that customers can warm before requesting playback. Cloud Spanner backs request operations with single-digit-millisecond responses, while BigQuery combines pipeline data for analysis of system performance and customer usage. Terraform on Google Cloud automates deployment of the stack across regions. The case does not name upstream media stores, external application integrations, or the specific vision models.
